items.definition:
a tendency to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen
His constant pessimism made it difficult to work with him.

a plant with large leaves and edible red or green stalks, often used in desserts
My grandmother makes a delicious rhubarb crumble.

a machine or device for shredding something, especially documents or garden waste
I need to buy a paper shredder for my old documents.

a type of comedy performance in which a comedian performs directly to the audience
We went to a standup show last night and it was hilarious.

a claw, especially of a bird of prey
The eagle gripped its prey firmly in its sharp talons.

a person who deliberately destroys or damages property
The police are looking for the vandals who spray-painted the wall.

a machine that helps a person breathe
The patient was placed on a ventilator to assist with breathing.

a faint design made in paper during manufacture
The document had a subtle watermark to prevent unauthorized copying.

a broadcast made on the internet
The company held a live webcast for its quarterly earnings report.

the time during which a broadcast is on air
The politician was given significant airtime to present his views.

the quality of being awesome
The sheer awesomeness of the Grand Canyon left them speechless.

the state of losing a loved one through death
She received many messages of sympathy during her time of bereavement.

a room where the board of directors of a company meets
Important decisions are made in the boardroom during weekly meetings.

a long-bladed hand tool with a bevelled cutting edge and a handle, used to cut or shape wood, stone, or metal
The sculptor used a chisel to carve the intricate details into the stone.

a small piece of partly burned coal or wood that has stopped glowing but is not yet ash
A hot cinder flew out of the fireplace and landed on the rug.

a large New World vulture, especially the California condor or Andean condor
The condor soared gracefully high above the mountain peaks.

sweets, candies, or pastries; the art or business of making them
The confectionery shop displayed an array of colorful chocolates and cakes.

a state of disorder or confusion
The room was in complete disarray after the party.

a fragrant herb with a distinctive anise-like flavor
She added sliced fennel to the salad.

practical work conducted in the natural environment
Anthropologists often spend years doing fieldwork.

excessive and insincere praise
He used flattery to try and get what he wanted.

the act of giving control or responsibility to another
The handover of power went smoothly.

an animal without a backbone
Worms and insects are examples of invertebrates.

a professional joker at a medieval court
The king's jester always made him laugh.

a gentle sheen or soft glow
The pearls had a beautiful luster.

A hormone that regulates sleep.
Many people take melatonin to help them sleep.

A person who lives in or uses a building or land.
The occupier of the apartment is responsible for paying the rent.

The quality of being practical or useful.
We need to consider the practicality of implementing such a large-scale project.

The action of delaying or postponing something.
Procrastination can lead to missed deadlines and increased stress.

fine sand, clay, or other material carried by running water and deposited as a sediment
The river deposited a layer of rich silt on the floodplains.

the state of being a sister; a bond between women
There was a strong sense of sisterhood among the women in the group.

a person who believes that their tastes in a particular area are superior to those of other people
He's such a coffee snob, he only drinks artisanal blends.

a poem of fourteen lines using any of a number of formal rhyme schemes
Shakespeare wrote many famous sonnets.

a tall tropical grass with thick, woody stems from which sugar is extracted
Sugarcane is a major crop in many tropical countries.

a person or thing that swings; a person who is lively and fashionable
The child was a natural swinger on the playground.

the state or quality of being tight
She felt a tightness in her chest due to anxiety.

wild animals that are believed to be harmful to crops, farm animals, or game, or that carry disease
The old house was infested with vermin.

a small gadget or mechanical device
This new app has a useful widget for tracking your steps.

a member of the aboriginal people of Australia
The history of the Aborigine people is rich and complex.

a short, traditional saying
The old adage 'haste makes waste' is still true today.

a substance that inhibits oxidation
Blueberries are rich in antioxidants, which are good for your health.

a person whose business is to take bets
He placed a bet with the bookie on the horse race.

the ability or tendency to float in water or air
The boat's buoyancy kept it afloat even in rough seas.

a person who has captured a person or animal
The police negotiated with the captor for the release of the hostages.

a living creature; an animal (informal)
There's a little critter scurrying under the porch.

an elaborate and spectacular entertainment or production
The New Year's Eve show was a dazzling musical extravaganza.

something given free of charge
They offered a freebie with every purchase to attract more customers.

the process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale
Globalisation has led to increased interconnectedness between economies worldwide.

the state of being unable to be seen
The magician created an illusion of invisibility.

a type of short trousers gathered at the knee (often plural 'knickers' for underwear)
He wore knickerbockers for his cycling trip.

a fictional weapon from Star Wars, a sword-like weapon made of light
Luke Skywalker wielded a blue lightsaber.

a large or important church, especially one that was formerly a monastery church
York Minster is a magnificent cathedral in England.

a type of grape or wine
The muscat grapes are very sweet and aromatic.

a device that makes a popping sound; a type of fastener
The party popper burst with confetti.

a female priest
The ancient temple was served by a high priestess.

a type of edible shellfish
We ordered pan-seared scallops for dinner.

the act of calming or making someone sleepy by administering a sedative drug
The patient was given light sedation before the procedure.

a person with a fiery temper; a type of British fighter aircraft
She's a real spitfire, always ready for an argument.

a small, pale soft-bodied insect that lives in large colonies
Termites can cause significant damage to wooden structures.

a lever used to turn the rudder of a boat; a machine for breaking up soil
He gripped the tiller firmly as the boat turned.

a person who traps wild animals, especially for their fur
The trapper set his snares deep in the forest.

the practice of using tricks or deception
He won the game through clever trickery.

A type of headwear consisting of a long piece of cloth wound around the head.
He wore a colorful turban as part of his traditional attire.

A long, pointed tooth, especially one that protrudes from the mouth of an animal.
The elephant's tusks were impressive.
